description: Savor the profound depths of Oaxacan Black Mole, a culinary masterpiece from southern Mexico. This iconic Mole Negro boasts a complex symphony of flavors, achieved through a meticulous blend of various chiles, spices, nuts, seeds, and a hint of Mexican chocolate. Prepare for a truly authentic taste experience that is rich, smoky, subtly sweet, and wonderfully savory, perfect for special occasions.

ingredients.notes: stems and seeds removed, for smokiness

instructions.title: Prepare and Rehydrate Chiles
instructions.text: Toast the mulato, ancho, pasilla, and chipotle chiles in a dry comal or large skillet over medium heat for about 30 seconds per side, until fragrant. Be careful not to burn them, as this will make the mole bitter. Transfer the toasted chiles to a bowl, cover completely with hot water, and let them rehydrate for 20-30 minutes until soft and pliable. Once rehydrated, drain the chiles, reserving some of the soaking liquid for later use if needed.

instructions.title: Roast and Fry Aromatics and Spices
instructions.text: In a skillet with a little oil, char the tomatillos, tomatoes, onion, and garlic until softened and slightly browned; set them aside. In the same skillet, fry the sliced ripe plantain until golden brown; remove and set aside. Next, lightly toast the almonds, pecans, sesame seeds, pumpkin seeds, raisins, cinnamon stick, whole cloves, black peppercorns, anise seeds, dried thyme, and Mexican oregano. Toast until fragrant, being careful not to burn. Remove and combine with the other toasted ingredients. Finally, fry the slice of day-old bread until golden.

instructions.title: Blend the Mole Paste
instructions.text: Combine the rehydrated chiles, roasted vegetables (tomatillos, tomatoes, onion, garlic), fried plantain, toasted nuts, seeds, raisins, spices, and fried bread in a blender. Add 2 cups of chicken broth. Blend the mixture until it is as smooth as possible. This may require blending in batches, depending on your blender's capacity. For the authentic silky texture, strain the blended mixture through a fine-mesh sieve into a large bowl, pressing down on any solids with the back of a spoon to extract all the liquid. Discard any remaining fibrous solids.

instructions.title: Cook the Mole Base
instructions.text: Heat the lard or vegetable oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium heat. Carefully pour in the strained mole paste. Cook, stirring constantly with a wooden spoon or spatula, for at least 30-45 minutes. This is a crucial step for developing the deep, rich flavor of the mole. The paste will darken significantly, thicken, and the oil will begin to separate, indicating it is properly cooked and the flavors have deepened.

instructions.title: Simmer and Finish the Mole
instructions.text: Gradually stir in the remaining chicken broth, about 1 cup at a time, allowing the mole to come to a gentle simmer after each addition. Continue adding broth until the mole reaches your desired consistency; it should be thick enough to coat the back of a spoon. Add the disc of Mexican chocolate and stir continuously until it completely melts and is fully incorporated into the mole sauce, lending its distinctive flavor and richness.

instructions.title: Season and Serve
instructions.text: Season the mole with salt and sugar to taste. The sugar helps to balance the bitterness from the chiles and chocolate. If the mole is too thick, add a little more broth or the reserved chile soaking liquid; if it's too thin, simmer uncovered for a bit longer to reduce. Serve the hot Mole Negro generously over cooked chicken, turkey, or pork, and garnish with a sprinkle of sesame seeds. Best served with warm tortillas and Mexican rice.

tips: For an authentic smoky flavor, ensure your chiles are properly toasted but not burnt; burnt chiles will make the mole bitter. A dry comal or cast-iron skillet works best.

Straining the mole paste through a fine-mesh sieve is crucial for achieving the silky-smooth texture characteristic of a true Oaxacan mole. Do not skip this step, as it significantly impacts the final result.
Mole Negro often improves with age. Make it a day ahead and gently reheat before serving to allow the complex flavors to meld and deepen further, making for an even more exquisite dish.
article:
The heart of Mexican cuisine beats with a rhythm of ancient traditions, vibrant flavors, and dishes that tell stories spanning centuries. Among these culinary masterpieces, none command as much respect and awe as mole. And when it comes to mole, there is one that reigns supreme, a dish so complex, so deeply flavored, and so culturally significant that it’s often referred to as the "king" of all moles: Oaxacan Black Mole, or Mole Negro.

This isn't just a sauce; it's a culinary journey, an exploration of sweet, savory, smoky, and spicy notes all harmoniously interwoven. Making authentic Oaxacan Black Mole is a labor of love, a commitment to a process that transforms dozens of humble ingredients into an extraordinary experience. If you’re ready to embark on a truly authentic Mexican dinner recipe adventure, prepare to be captivated by the magic of Mole Negro.

## What is Oaxacan Black Mole (Mole Negro)?

Oaxacan Black Mole, known locally as Mole Negro, hails from the southern Mexican state of Oaxaca, a region renowned for its rich culinary heritage and diverse moles. While there are seven major moles attributed to Oaxaca, Mole Negro stands out for its characteristic deep, almost inky black color and its unparalleled depth of flavor. This isn't a dish you whip up on a weeknight; it's a celebratory meal, often prepared for weddings, baptisms, Day of the Dead, and other significant family gatherings.

The dark hue of Oaxacan Black Mole comes from a careful selection and preparation of several types of dried chiles, which are toasted, charred, and rehydrated to bring out their complex notes. But the chiles are only the beginning. The ingredient list is extensive, often exceeding 20 or even 30 components, including nuts, seeds, spices, fruits, aromatic vegetables, and, crucially, Mexican chocolate. Each ingredient plays a vital role, contributing a layer of flavor that builds into a symphony for the palate – smoky, earthy, subtly sweet, a touch spicy, and incredibly rich. It's a testament to the ingenuity of Oaxacan cooks who masterfully balance these elements to create a sauce that is both ancient and timeless.

## Ingredients You'll Need for Authentic Mole Negro

Preparing authentic Oaxacan Black Mole requires a trip to a well-stocked Mexican grocery store or a good online purveyor. Don't be intimidated by the long list; each item contributes to the final, magnificent flavor.

**The Chiles (the backbone):**
*   **6-8 Ancho chiles:** Large, mild, dark, fruity.
*   **6-8 Mulato chiles:** Similar to ancho but darker, smoky, slightly sweet.
*   **6-8 Pasilla chiles:** Long, thin, dark, with a mild, earthy flavor.
*   **2-3 Chipotle chiles (optional for extra heat/smokiness):** Small, wrinkled, very smoky and spicy.

**Nuts and Seeds (for thickening and richness):**
*   1/2 cup raw almonds
*   1/2 cup raw peanuts
*   1/4 cup sesame seeds
*   2 tablespoons pumpkin seeds (pepitas)
*   1/4 cup raisins or prunes

**Spices and Aromatics (the soul):**
*   1 large white onion, roughly chopped
*   6-8 cloves garlic
*   1 plantain (ripe, yellow with black spots), sliced
*   2-3 Roma tomatoes, roughly chopped
*   1/4 teaspoon whole cloves
*   1/4 teaspoon black peppercorns
*   1/4 teaspoon cumin seeds
*   1 stick Mexican cinnamon (about 2-3 inches)
*   1/2 teaspoon dried oregano (Mexican preferred)
*   Pinch of thyme
*   Pinch of anise seeds (optional)

**Thickeners and Sweeteners (the body and balance):**
*   2 stale corn tortillas or 1 slice of day-old bread (or even a few animal crackers for an authentic touch)
*   1-2 ounces Mexican chocolate (bittersweet, often with cinnamon)
*   1 tablespoon piloncillo (Mexican brown sugar cone), grated, or brown sugar to taste

**Other Essentials:**
*   1/2 cup lard or vegetable oil, divided
*   6-8 cups chicken broth (homemade is best)
*   Salt to taste
*   1 whole chicken, cut into pieces, or 4-6 chicken thighs/breasts

## Step-by-Step Instructions for Oaxacan Black Mole

Patience and attention to detail are your best allies in preparing this incredible Oaxacan Black Mole.

1.  **Prepare the Chiles:** Carefully remove stems and seeds from all dried chiles. Heat a dry comal or skillet over medium heat and toast the chiles in batches for 30 seconds to 1 minute per side until fragrant and slightly puffed, being careful not to burn them (burnt chiles will make the mole bitter). Immediately transfer to a bowl, cover with hot water, and let them rehydrate for 20-30 minutes until soft. Drain, reserving the soaking water.

2.  **Toast Nuts and Seeds:** In a separate dry skillet, toast the almonds, peanuts, sesame seeds, and pumpkin seeds individually until lightly golden and fragrant. Transfer to separate bowls.

3.  **Fry Aromatics and Fruits:** Heat 1/4 cup of lard or oil in a large pot or Dutch oven. Fry the onion, garlic, plantain, and tomatoes until softened and slightly caramelized. Transfer to a bowl. In the same oil, quickly fry the tortillas or bread until golden. Add to the bowl with the aromatics.

4.  **Grind Spices:** Lightly toast the whole cloves, peppercorns, cumin seeds, cinnamon stick, oregano, thyme, and anise seeds (if using) in the dry skillet until fragrant.

5.  **Blend into a Paste:** Combine the rehydrated chiles, toasted nuts, seeds, fried aromatics, fried tortillas/bread, and toasted spices in a blender. Add 1-2 cups of fresh chicken broth or the reserved chile soaking water (strained) to help blend. Blend on high until a very smooth paste forms. This may require working in batches and blending for several minutes, stopping to scrape down the sides. A truly smooth paste is crucial.

6.  **Cook the Mole:** Heat the remaining 1/4 cup of lard or oil in the large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat. Carefully pour in the mole paste (it will splatter, so be cautious). Cook the paste, stirring constantly, for at least 30-45 minutes. This step is vital for developing the flavor and achieving the deep color. The paste will thicken and darken significantly.

7.  **Simmer and Season:** Gradually add the remaining chicken broth, stirring constantly to prevent lumps. Bring the mole to a gentle simmer. Add the Mexican chocolate and piloncillo (or brown sugar), stirring until melted and fully incorporated. Season generously with salt. Continue to simmer the mole, uncovered, for at least 1 to 2 hours, stirring occasionally, allowing the flavors to meld and the sauce to thicken to your desired consistency. If it becomes too thick, add a little more broth or water.

8.  **Prepare the Protein:** While the mole simmers, cook your chicken. You can boil, poach, or roast the chicken until tender. Shred or cut into serving pieces.

9.  **Combine and Serve:** Add the cooked chicken pieces directly into the simmering Oaxacan Black Mole during the last 30 minutes of cooking, allowing them to absorb the rich flavors.

## Expert Tips for the Best Mole Negro

*   **Patience is Paramount:** Making Oaxacan Black Mole is a multi-hour process. Don't rush any step, especially the toasting of ingredients and the simmering of the paste. Each stage contributes to the final depth of flavor.
*   **Quality Ingredients:** Seek out authentic Mexican ingredients, particularly the chiles and Mexican chocolate. The difference in flavor is palpable.
*   **Blender Power:** A high-speed blender is your best friend for achieving a super smooth mole paste. If you only have a regular blender, you may need to strain the mole through a fine-mesh sieve after blending to remove any remaining bits of chile skin or seeds.
*   **Taste and Adjust:** Mole is all about balance. Taste frequently and adjust seasonings – salt, sugar, and even a touch of acidity (like a squeeze of lime or a splash of vinegar) can brighten the flavors.
*   **Make Ahead:** Mole often tastes even better the next day, as the flavors have more time to meld. It also freezes beautifully for future meals.
*   **Don't Burn the Chiles:** This is the most common pitfall. Burnt chiles will impart a bitter, acrid taste to your entire mole. Toast them gently until fragrant, not smoking.

## Serving Suggestions for Your Mole

Oaxacan Black Mole is typically served as a main course, most famously with chicken or turkey.

*   **Traditional:** Ladle generous portions of the rich Oaxacan Black Mole over tender pieces of chicken or turkey. Serve alongside fluffy white rice and warm, freshly made corn tortillas.
*   **Other Proteins:** While chicken is classic, Mole Negro also pairs wonderfully with pork (especially slow-cooked pork shoulder), duck, or even roasted vegetables for a vegetarian option.
*   **Sides:** Beyond rice and tortillas, consider serving refried beans, or a simple green salad to cut through the richness.
*   **Garnish:** A sprinkle of toasted sesame seeds and a few sprigs of fresh cilantro add a lovely visual and textural contrast.
*   **Beverage Pairings:** Agua frescas, Mexican beer, or a medium-bodied red wine can complement the complex flavors.

## Variations and Common Questions

The world of mole is vast and varied. While Oaxacan Black Mole is arguably the most famous, Oaxaca alone boasts six other major moles: Rojo (red), Verde (green), Amarillo (yellow), Coloradito (little red), Manchamanteles (tablecloth stainer), and Chichilo. Each has its unique flavor profile, color, and list of ingredients. Our recipe today focuses on the pinnacle of these, the majestic Mole Negro.

**Common Questions:**

*   **Can I make it vegetarian?** Absolutely! Substitute chicken broth with vegetable broth and serve the mole over roasted root vegetables, plantains, or even hearty mushrooms.
*   **How long does Mole Negro keep?** Stored in an airtight container, it will last 5-7 days in the refrigerator. It freezes exceptionally well for up to 3-4 months, making it perfect for meal prep.
*   **Is Oaxacan Black Mole very spicy?** While it contains several chiles, the heat level is usually balanced by the other ingredients. It's more about complex flavor than overwhelming spice. You can adjust the number of chipotle chiles to control the heat.
*   **Where can I find specific ingredients like Mexican chocolate or piloncillo?** Most larger supermarkets now have international aisles, but a dedicated Mexican grocery store or online retailers will have the best selection of authentic chiles and other specialty items.

Embarking on the journey to make Oaxacan Black Mole is more than just cooking; it's an experience, a connection to a profound culinary tradition. The reward for your effort will be an unforgettable meal, a truly authentic Mexican dinner recipe that will transport your taste buds straight to the heart of Oaxaca. Enjoy the process, savor the aroma, and delight in the unparalleled flavor of this magnificent dish.
